transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. AI. What brings you in today?

I’m here because nobody seems to take it seriously that people at work are secretly targeting my projects, even when I show them the evidence. It’s incredibly frustrating that everyone just dismisses what is clearly going on right in front of them.
Have you ever heard voices or seen things that other people could not, or had a sudden period where these beliefs came on very quickly over days to weeks?

No, I’ve never heard voices or seen things that aren't there—my senses are perfectly fine. This didn't happen overnight either; it started about a year ago during a major cloud migration project and gradually became clearer to me over the course of nine months.
Before this started, have you generally been suspicious and distrustful of other people in many areas of your life, or did this begin only around the work situation?

No, I’ve never been a suspicious or distrustful person in general; this is strictly about that competing team at work targeting my projects. Outside of trying to protect my code from them, my life is completely normal. I trust people just fine, like my cousin who I still meet up with for pho every weekend.
Aside from this belief about your coworkers, has it caused any other major problems in your life, such as changes in your mood, sleep, work performance, or relationships?

I still handle my day-to-day responsibilities just fine, like fixing my tickets, helping junior devs, and paying my bills on time. However, HR has warned me that my accusations in meetings are putting my job at risk, and I've stopped going to team events and playing basketball because I'm constantly on guard. Outside of work, my life is mostly normal, but this situation has definitely strained my professional relationships.
Have you ever had any other unusual beliefs outside of work, or any periods of depression, high energy, decreased need for sleep, or feeling unusually sped up?

No, I’ve never had any other unusual beliefs, and my mood and sleep have been completely normal without any periods of depression or high energy. My only issue is protecting my code from being sabotaged by that other team at work. I just want people to actually look at the evidence I have.
Have you ever believed that the same people are also trying to harm, monitor, or interfere with you outside of work, or is it limited only to the workplace?

Yes, I do believe that competing team has been monitoring my personal accounts outside of work to find ways to make me look bad. But even with them snooping, it hasn't stopped me from managing my life normally, like paying my bills on time or meeting up with my cousin.
Have you noticed any decline in your overall functioning outside of the work situation, such as trouble managing finances, self-care, or relationships because of these beliefs?

No, my functioning outside of work is completely fine; I pay my bills on time, take care of myself, and meet my cousin for pho every weekend. The only real change is that I've pulled back from late-night basketball and social events because I have to stay on guard. Other than that, my day-to-day life is completely normal.
Have you ever had any other unusual beliefs outside of this situation, such as feeling specially chosen, being controlled, or believing messages are hidden in ordinary events?

No, I've never felt specially chosen, controlled, or that there are hidden messages in everyday things. My only concern is the very real, specific pattern of sabotage by that competing tech team at my work. There's nothing else going on besides me trying to protect my code.
Have you ever had any other psychotic symptoms, such as hearing voices, seeing things others do not, or believing your thoughts are being controlled or broadcast to others?

No, I don't hear voices, see things that aren't there, or feel like my thoughts are being controlled or broadcast at all. My mind is completely clear. My only concern is the very real, logical pattern of sabotage that I can see in my work logs.
Have you ever considered that there might be another explanation for what’s happening at work, or are you completely certain the competing team is targeting you even when others disagree?

I am absolutely certain because the patterns in the logs and the timing of the glitches are far too precise to be coincidences. Even though IT and my manager claim they can't find anything, they simply aren't looking closely enough or don't understand the pattern like I do. There is no other logical explanation.

Have you ever been able to consider that this might be a misunderstanding or something other than deliberate targeting, even briefly, or are you completely convinced it is true despite what others say?

No, it is definitely not a misunderstanding because the evidence in the logs and the timing of the glitches are just too clear to ignore. Even though IT and management claim they can't find anything, I am completely convinced that the other team is targeting me. There is simply no other way to explain what is happening.
Has this belief ever led you to take actions like confronting, reporting, or trying to retaliate against the people you think are targeting you?

Yes, I did speak up during a sprint review meeting and accused a colleague from that team of spying on my work. It wasn't about retaliation, I was just pointing out the truth, but HR intervened and warned me that my position on the project is now at risk.
Have these beliefs about being targeted lasted continuously for at least 1 month, and have they stayed limited to this one topic without other psychotic symptoms?

Yes, this has been going on continuously for about nine months now, and it is strictly focused on that other team sabotaging my work and tracking my accounts. I don't experience any other unusual things like hearing voices, and my mind is completely clear—I still handle my daily tickets, pay my bills, and see my cousin every weekend.
Has this belief ever spread into other areas of your life outside work, or has it stayed focused only on the competing team and your projects?

No, it has stayed completely focused on that competing team and my projects. Outside of defending my work from them, my life is entirely normal; I still handle my tickets, help junior devs, and pay my bills on time. I even meet up with my cousin for pho every weekend just like I always have.
